Vehicle damage

Car damaged? What now?

This is general information, not legal advice. HRM’s pages describe how to start an incident report; they do not promise a claim outcome.

  1. Stay safe

    HRM’s 311 page says to call 911 when immediate help is needed because health, safety, or property is threatened.

    Checked on 25 November 2026. HRM: 311 Municipal Services and Information.

  2. Photos

    HRM’s checked pothole and 311 pages do not say whether photos are required. Confirm current requirements with HRM or your insurer.

    Checked on 25 November 2026. HRM: Potholes and Sinkholes.

  3. Date and place

    HRM’s claim information does not say exactly what details you must provide. HRM’s online pothole form asks for a street address (called a “civic address” on the form). This site does not collect or forward addresses.

    Checked on 25 November 2026. HRM: Potholes and Sinkholes.

  4. Contact whoever maintains the road

    For roads maintained by the Province, including 100-series highways, HRM directs residents to call 511. For a pothole on an HRM-maintained road, HRM says to call 311 to start a report about the damage.

    Checked on 25 November 2026. HRM: Potholes and Sinkholes.

  5. What happens next

    HRM says a report made through 311 is sent to the right team. Staff typically get in touch in about 10 business days. This is not a guaranteed response time or claim outcome.

    Checked on 25 November 2026. HRM: Potholes and Sinkholes.

  6. What to expect

    HRM’s public pages do not say who is at fault, whether you qualify for compensation, or what will happen with an individual claim. Use HRM’s official process for current information.

    Checked on 25 November 2026. HRM: Potholes and Sinkholes.
